summary: Live check 2 after wave 7: three journeys with the real model and forerunner-sandbox (cap USD 7.25), then a code-level verification of each finding

steps.step: GitHub token typed into the setup assistant's GitHub step (Playwright from env, no screenshot while the field held it)
steps.observed: The daemon's check failed for environment reasons. Direct (no proxy): GitHub answered 401 Bad credentials for FORERUNNER_TEST_GITHUB_TOKEN. Through the agent proxy (NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1): the proxy swaps in this session's own GitHub App credentials for any token, even an invalid one, and blocks GET /user/repos ('sessions are bound to their configured repositories'). The app then said 'Token needs changes before it can be used. Classic token lacks the repo scope. Could not list the repositories the token reaches (GET /user/repos returned 403)'. Workaround: the token was written straight into the bench vault (scripts/vault-gh.mts, value never printed). The daemon was restarted with --env NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1, then setup was finished in the UI ('GitHub is connected'). So every GitHub action ran on the proxy-injected identity (joelwellbournewood). The proxy also appends '_Generated by Claude Code_' to every PR body and comment.

findings.title: Chain of three, busy middle: the last PR gets a false conflict card and stays blocked after it was rebuilt cleanly
findings.what_the_person_sees: After squash-merging the first PR of a chain A <- B <- C while B's folder has a stray file, C's Overview row reads '#15 could not be rebuilt without #13, which was merged: both change kite/events.html. It waits for you: redo the task, or resolve it on GitHub.' It has no Merge, and the Inbox has a card with Redo / Leave it open. C only changes kite/index.html. Once the file is removed, B and C are rebuilt correctly on GitHub (#15 mergeable, clean, 'Builds on #14'). The row and card stayed as they were for over 50 minutes and several polls, through #14's merge, until the end of the run. The Tasks tab says 'Accepted · waiting for you to merge' for the same task, so the screens disagree.
findings.expected: R-chain: while B's folder is busy, C is not rebuilt onto B's old head. Both records wait for the person with no card, and after B is rebuilt C follows it. At the latest, once C is rebuilt cleanly, its conflict sentence and card go away and Merge comes back.
findings.evidence: steps/43-chain2-overview-after-squash-dirty.txt, 44-chain2-overview-after-rebuild.txt, 45-chain2-inbox-after-rebuild.txt, 46-chain2-tasks-after-rebuild.txt. evidence/chain2-after-squash-dirty.json and chain2-after-clean.json (#15 = 36a6cc0, 6c39e98, 732282f). daemon.log: 03:57:59 'dependent branch not rebuilt: its worktree has uncommitted changes' (B), 03:59:16 B rebuilt, 03:59:22 C rebuilt with dropped [13:copied] and kept [14]. Then /projects/:id/pull-requests still had #15 state blocked with the conflict sentence at 03:59:55, 04:02:23 and 04:50; GitHub reported #15 mergeable true/clean.
findings.repro: Repository project, You press Merge. Tasks: A 'Write kite/events.html'; B 'Add a third event to kite/events.html' (waits on A, changes A's file); C 'Link kite/events.html from kite/index.html' (waits on B, changes only index.html). Run the session. Put scratch.txt into <home>/worktrees/<B id>/. Squash-merge A's PR on GitHub. After one poll, C's row and card show the false conflict. Remove scratch.txt and wait for the next poll: B and C are rebuilt on GitHub, but C's row and card never clear.
findings.suspected_cause: PrTaskExecutor.rebuildDependents adds a task to `changed` only when it was 'rebuilt'. A busy B is skipped while C is still rebuilt against A, so the rebuild conflicts on B's events.html change. The later successful rebuild's settleRecord moves the record only when r.voids or ownBefore/ownAfter differ. Nothing clears last_outcome 'rebuild_conflict' or the card once the rebuild succeeds.

findings.title: Status pull request setting writes into another project's open status PR on the shared fr/status branch
findings.what_the_person_sees: With 'Status pull request' on for Kite shop, the session's status was pushed to fr/status and commented on PR #5 'docs: project status'. #5 is an open PR another project ('Sandbox hello page', 2026-11-02) opened. The commit replaced that project's Done list in docs/status.md with Kite shop's tasks. Kite shop's Overview now offers '"Project status (docs/status.md)" · pull request #5' with Merge. A person who merges it merges two projects' status history into one file. Two projects on the same repository with the setting on would overwrite each other's status.
findings.expected: A project's status PR is its own: a per-project branch, or one that is not reused when another project's PR is on it. The Overview lists only this project's status PR, as L-16 does for docs PRs.
findings.evidence: daemon.log 04:49:57 '[project-docs] status update written {projectId: 01a1be6b-b649..., branch: fr/status, prUrl: .../pull/5, committed: true}'. git diff 6759c4b..152f5ac on origin/fr/status: '- Add a footer to the hello page / - Check the page and README section / ...' replaced by '+ Add the line Bye to shop/bye.txt / + Write the kite size guide in shop/ ...'. #5 comment 2026-11-09T04:49:57Z 'Status update of session 01a1bea3-...'. steps/160-c57-status-p2-overview.txt.
findings.repro: On a repository that already has an open 'docs: project status' PR on fr/status from another project or an earlier install, link a project, set Settings > Other settings > '<project> Status pull request' to On, and run any session. The status commit lands on the other PR and the Overview lists that PR.
findings.suspected_cause: The status branch name is fixed ('fr/status'), not per project, and the status writer reuses the open PR on that head without checking which project it belongs to.

findings.title: Two open cards for one conflict after a Tasks-tab Redo; the conflict notice is not withdrawn when the rework resolves it
findings.what_the_person_sees: Two open Inbox cards for one problem on the same task: '"Write a motto in kite/motto.txt" conflicts with main' (Redo / Leave it open) and '"Write a motto in kite/motto.txt" conflicts with main in kite/motto.txt; the agent could…' (I resolved it / Drop the branch / Cancel). After the person resolved it and the task went back to Done with #19 mergeable (04:19:56), the first card stayed open. It was still open at 04:21:16, when another merge made #19 conflict again.
findings.expected: One card per conflict (R-conflict: 'exactly one card'). A Redo or a resolution answers or withdraws the conflict notice, and it shows under Answered once the PR is mergeable.
findings.evidence: steps/82-tm2-and-b2-inbox.txt; /inbox at 04:19:58 and 04:20:45 listing both. daemon.log has no 'conflict resolved' line for #19.
findings.repro: Get a conflict notice card on a done task (merge another PR changing the same lines). Press Redo on that task's row in the Tasks tab and Start session: the rebase-conflict card is filed beside the open conflict notice. Resolve it in the folder, answer 'I resolved it' and Start. The task is Done, but the conflict notice stays open.
findings.suspected_cause: The rework path files its own conflict request without settling the watcher's conflict-notice request for the same task.

findings.title: Merge answers 'Merging #23.' although the merge cannot run (owed rebuild on a dirty folder)
findings.what_the_person_sees: Pressing Merge on #23, whose folder had uncommitted changes known since 04:14:34, showed 'Merging #23.' first. A few seconds later the row changed to '#23 waits for changes left in its task's folder: take them out or redo the task.'
findings.expected: The answer says at once why it waits (design §5 rule 9: no promise the code does not keep), as the row then does.
findings.evidence: steps/71-tm4-merge23-right-after.txt ('Merging #23.'), 74-tm4-merge23-after-12s.txt; evidence/tm4-merge23-answer.json {state: queued, sentence: 'Merging #23.'}
findings.repro: Chain A <- B. Put a file in B's task folder, close A's PR, wait one poll, press Merge on B's Overview row.
findings.suspected_cause: The merge route queues before reading the record's owed-rebuild/folder state; the merge step finds it later.

findings.title: Conflict notices appear and clear only after about two polls (about 2 min), with Merge still offered meanwhile
findings.what_the_person_sees: After another merge made PRs conflict, the rows kept offering Merge for 1 min 47 s (R-conflict) and about 2 min (TM-7) before the conflict sentence appeared. Clearing it after main was put back also took 2 min 13 s. A Merge pressed in that window would fail.

findings.evidence: Squash #16 at 04:14:10, conflicts logged at 04:15:57-58. README change pushed at 04:22:28, #23 conflict at 04:24:36. Title restored at 04:24:48, rebuilt-without sentence back at 04:27:01.

verified.root_cause:
Two defects in the app's logic, which together give what the person saw. The model is not involved: the three tasks did what they were asked.

1) The false conflict (pr-executor.ts:1705-1708, with 1649-1651). `rebuildDependents` rebuilds the chain in depth order and adds a task to `changed` only when it was rebuilt. A middle task B that comes back `busy` (its folder has uncommitted changes, so `rebuildIn` returns busy) does not stop the tasks that build on it. C is still rebuilt in the same pass, because it holds A. `rebuildBranch` finds A `copied` and B `open` (kept), and `dependencyBase` merges B's old, unrebuilt branch onto main. That branch still holds A's original commits, and main now has A's squash. When B changed A's file, this is an add/add conflict on kite/events.html, so the rebuild returns `after: null` with that file in `conflicts`. `settleRecord` (dependent-branches.ts:633-641) then moves C's record to `left_to_you` with `last_outcome: "rebuild_conflict"` and `rebuildConflictSentence`, and files the card. The sentence blames C ("#15 could not be rebuilt without #13 ... both change kite/events.html"), but the conflict is between B's old head and main, not C's own change. The existing R-chain test (dependent-branches-merge.test.ts:450) gives each task its own file, so this path never conflicts there.

2) The conflict never clears (dependent-branches.ts:653-659). Once B's folder is clean, the sweep rebuilds B and then C (C follows B through `rebuiltTo`, and the own change is the same). `settleRecord` takes the same-own-change branch, which only moves `reviewed_head_sha` and `own_change_id` and keeps state, sentence and `last_outcome` ("rebuild_conflict"). The open card is not touched. Nothing else clears it: `conflictNotice` takes a notice back only when `last_outcome === "conflict"` (line 285), and skips `rebuild_conflict` (324-325). `closeConflictCard` skips cards that carry `rebuild` (506). `pull-requests.ts:167` lists `rebuild_conflict` in `NO_CLICK`, so the Overview row stays `blocked` with no Merge. The Tasks label is built from the task, not the record, so it still says "Accepted · waiting for you to merge", which is why the two screens disagree.

Reproduced on the stand-in (FakeGitHost, real git, the runner, ReviewedPrMerge, GitHostWatcher and DependentBranches composed as in dependent-branches-merge.test.ts). Two parts. Each one alone fixes the person's view of this journey; both are needed for the general case.

(a) Prevent the false conflict (R-chain), in `PrTaskExecutor.rebuildDependents`. Keep a set `blocked` of task ids whose outcome in this pass was busy, held, failed or conflict. If any of them is in `blocked`, return `{ taskId, prNumber: null, prUrl: null, result: "busy" }` without touching its folder, and add it to `blocked` too, so a chain of four stops as well. The runtime's `settleOwed` then keeps C owed (`rebuild_owed_for` = A). R-lock holds C's Merge, `conflictNotice` stays quiet because a rebuild is owed, and no card is filed. The next sweep rebuilds B, then C (`changed` now includes B), and both wait for the person on their new heads with no card. This is the outcome test (c) already expects.

- The same-own-change branch moves the record to the new head as now, and also says again what the record said before the conflict. Keep it on the conflict card as `before_conflict`, as TM-7 does for the conflict notice. With nothing kept, use the mode's normal wait: `not_allowed` with "#N waits for you to merge it: press Merge on the Overview."
- Withdraw the card whose `change_card.rebuild === "conflict"`, or restore the card it took over.
- The `voids` and own-change-changed branches already replace the sentence and card.

verified.root_cause:
The finding is real, and the model had no part in it. The status pull request belongs to the repository, not to a project. There are three causes.

1. The branch name is fixed. `STATUS_BRANCH = "fr/status"` (packages/runtime/src/loop/docs.ts:100) is the same for every project and every install. `writeSessionStatus` always uses it (docs.ts:800).

2. The writer reuses whatever pull request it finds. `checkout` takes the first open PR whose head is the branch (docs.ts:970-973: `listPullRequests(..., {state:"open", head: branch})[0]`) and never asks whose it is. `writeSessionStatus` then passes `fresh: (open) => !open` (docs.ts:802-805). With any open PR on fr/status, the clone starts from `origin/fr/status`, which here was the other project's branch. Next, `writeStatusUpdate` → `applyStatusUpdate` (packages/memory/src/docs.ts:339-354) rewrites the Done, In flight, Blocked and Next lists from this project's tasks and adds this project's session to the other project's history. The push is a normal push because `force: !existingPr` (docs.ts:812). Finally `commentOnPullRequest(existingPr.number, ...)` comments on the other project's PR (docs.ts:814-815). The status PR body says nothing about which project it is for (docs.ts:821, no `scaffoldProjectLine`), so no ownership check is possible today.

3. The Overview ownership test approves any fr/status PR. `isProjectDocsPr` returns `statusPullRequestOn(project)` for any PR whose head is fr/status (docs.ts:146). With the setting on, every project on the repository counts that PR as its own. The Overview row (packages/runtime/src/daemon/pull-requests.ts:392, titled by `docsTitle` at :70) and `docsInPullRequests` (docs.ts:888-891) therefore list it with Merge. ADR 0106 point 5 records this rule as part of L-16. L-16 fixed the same problem for scaffold PRs but treated the status PR as owned by whoever has the setting on.

The evidence matches. In /tmp/frbench/live2/github/work/sandbox, `git diff 6759c4b..152f5ac` shows commit 152f5ac, "docs: status after session 01a1bea3" (Kite shop, 2026-11-09). It sits on top of 6759c4b, "docs: status after session 01a19c97" (2026-11-02, another project). It replaces the "Add a footer to the hello page / Check the page and README section / Add index.html..." Done list with Kite shop's four tasks, and it keeps the 2026-11-02 session history beneath its own entry. daemon.log:297 logs `branch fr/status, prUrl .../pull/5, committed: true` for project 01a1be6b. Step 160-c57-status-p2-overview.txt lists '"Project status (docs/status.md)" · pull request #5 · Merge' under "Forerunner's docs".

Give each project its own status branch and record the owner on the PR, as L-16 did for the scaffold.

1. Name the branch per project, e.g. `statusBranch(project) = "fr/status-" + safeSegment(project.id, "project")`, the same way the intake's `fr/intake-<id>-docs` is named. Use it in `writeSessionStatus`.

2. Accept both names in `isDocsBranch`: match `^fr/status(-[^/]+)?$`. Update `docsTitle` (pull-requests.ts:70) so either branch reads "Project status (docs/status.md)".

3. In `isProjectDocsPr`, count a status PR as this project's only when its branch is this project's status branch and the setting is on. For a legacy `fr/status` PR, require its body to contain `scaffoldProjectLine(project)`. Otherwise return false, so another project's or an earlier install's PR is never listed or merged from this Overview.

4. End the status PR body with `scaffoldProjectLine(project)` ("Forerunner project <id>.").

5. Before reusing `existingPr` in `writeSessionStatus`, check `isProjectDocsPr(project, existingPr)`. When the check fails, never push to or comment on that PR: start this project's own branch from the default branch.

6. Amend ADR 0106 points 3 and 5 and the maintainer doc for loop/docs.

Options are to write the status PR only when `.forerunner/project.json` marks the repository as this project's (otherwise keep the status in the app and say so in the setting), or to use a per-project path.

verified.root_cause:
Two gaps together leave the watcher's conflict notice open.

(1) The Tasks tab's Redo (the `task.reopen` command, then `personMove`) skips the task's open merge card. For a done task it withdraws nothing, because WAITS_ON_CARDS (task.ts:93) is needs_human, failed and in_review, and the withdraw at :440 only covers those or a cancel. It also does not mark `redo_from_base` the way the card's own Redo does (`applyRedo`, pr-answers.ts:319-345, sets REDO_FROM_BASE_FIELD at :338). So the redo's run picks up the conflicting branch again. Its rebase onto main conflicts, and PrTaskExecutor files a second card, the githost:rebase_conflict card, next to the notice. That breaks "exactly one card" (R-conflict) and design §3.8 ("A card whose task has moved on is closed").

(2) When the rework finishes, the notice is never taken back. After the new review, the merge step's `settle` (merge.ts:1771-1774) moves the record with `last_outcome: outcome.status`, which is "not_allowed" under "You press Merge". That overwrites "conflict". `DependentBranches.conflictNotice` withdraws a card only when `record.last_outcome === "conflict"` (dependent-branches.ts:285, then closeConflictCard at :319/:503). So once main is mergeable again it returns false, and the card stays open with its Redo still live.

When #19 conflicted again at 04:24:35, `conflictCard` (:366) took over that stale card instead of filing a new one. It stored the card's own conflict words as `before_conflict.card`. If that conflict later goes away with the same head, `restoreCard` would bring the conflict words back rather than close the card.

The evidence and a stand-in repro both confirm this:
- state.sqlite from the live run: request 01a1be85 (merge:left_open, notice conflict) was created 04:15:58 and is still open. The two rebase_conflict cards (04:17:53, 04:19:19) were answered "I resolved it".
- daemon.log, line 195 (04:19:53): the merge step set #19's record to left_to_you/not_allowed, and there is no "merges cleanly again" line for #19.
- Scratch copy of the composed test (fake GitHub, real git, no model), with `taskReopen.run` called as source ui: after the Redo the notice is still open. After the session the task is needs_human with 2 cards (the notice plus "conflicts with main in index.html; the agent could not resolve it"). After "Drop the branch" and the rework, the task is done, #2 is mergeable, the record says not_allowed, and after two polls the notice is still open.

verified.root_cause:
The merge route decides what to answer before anything has checked the task's folder. The "folder holds changes" fact only reaches the merge record later, from the background merge step.

Order of events in the github journey (daemon.log, steps 71-74):
1. 04:14:31: #21 is closed.
2. 04:14:34: the rebuild of #23 finds uncommitted changes in its folder. pr-executor.ts:1793-1799 logs once, keeps the fact in memory (`heldByChanges`) and returns `result: "busy"`.
3. `DependentBranches.settleOwed` (dependent-branches.ts:~596) treats "busy" as owed. It sets only `rebuild_owed_for` on #23's record, which stays `left_to_you` with `last_outcome: "not_allowed"`. Nothing about the folder is persisted on the record.
4. The Overview row comes from `mergeOfRecord` (pull-requests.ts:205-235). It calls `owedWaitOf` -> `owedMergeWait` (merge-mode.ts:108-109), which says the wait only when state is `queued`/`waiting_checks` AND `last_outcome === OWED_FOLDER_CHANGES`. Neither holds, so the row offers Merge with no sentence (step 71 shows "Merge" on #23).
5. Under "You press Merge", the watcher's `retryWaiting` (merge.ts:977) only reads `queued`/`waiting_checks` records. So the merge step never looked at this folder before the press.
6. On the press, `ProjectPullRequests.merge` (pull-requests.ts:559-631) checks only `row.merge.canMerge` (true). It calls `approveInOrder` (merge.ts:1145, which sets queued, person approval, sentence "#23 merges now: you pressed Merge.") and answers `{state: "queued", sentence: "Merging #23."}` (pull-requests.ts:629). That matches evidence/tm4-merge23-answer.json.
7. Only then does the background `mergeApproved` -> `run` reach `if (record.rebuild_owed_for)` (merge.ts:1372). `sayOwedWait` (merge.ts:1894-1916) finds the folder dirty and writes `owed_folder_changes` plus the sentence. verified.root_cause:
The conflict notice depends only on the `mergeable` value that the git host watcher's scheduled poll reads. When GitHub returns null (it has not computed mergeability yet), that read is dropped, and nothing reads the pull request again before the next scheduled poll.

1. Each poll's read of an open task PR is stored in `DependentBranches.seen` (dependent-branches.ts:199). The end-of-poll sweep looks at it once and then deletes it (dependent-branches.ts:265).
2. `conflictNotice` returns early when `mergeable` is neither true nor false: `if (info.mergeable !== true && info.mergeable !== false) return false;` (dependent-branches.ts:277). This affects both giving the notice (false) and taking it back (true).
3. The watcher schedules the next poll only `pollMs` after the previous poll ends: `DEFAULT_GITHOST_POLL_MS = 60_000` (githost-watcher.ts:61), rescheduled at githost-watcher.ts:395. Nothing triggers a quick re-read.
4. Real GitHub computes mergeability lazily. The first GET after the base branch moves starts the computation and returns `mergeable: null`. So the first poll after a merge or push always gets null, and the value only arrives one full cycle later (about 60 s plus the poll's own time, roughly 70 s here).

The evidence matches exactly two cycles in all three cases:
- **#16 squash:** squashed at 04:14:10. The poll at 04:14:24 saw the merge (and a null for #17, #18, #19); the notices came at 04:15:57-58, 107 s after the squash.
- **README push:** pushed at 04:22:28. The poll at about 04:23:26 read null; the #23 notice came at 04:24:36, 128 s after the push.
- **Title restore:** restored at 04:24:48. The poll at about 04:25:46 read null; the notice was taken back at 04:26:57, 129 s after the restore.

The journey's own GitHub reads confirm GitHub returned null/"unknown" right after base changes in this run: rb-after.json (#23 at 04:22:15) and chain2-after-squash-dirty.json (#15).

The stand-in hides this. testenv/src/githost/ops.ts:351-373 (`computeMergeability`) works out mergeability eagerly on every ref change and GET, so it never returns null for an open PR. The R-conflict test (packages/runtime/test/dependent-branches-merge.test.ts:903) passes with "one card after one poll" (I re-ran it: green). It also reads the PR itself (`m.pr(b.id)`) before polling, which on real GitHub would itself start the computation.

verified.root_cause:
The finding is real, and the cause is in the code. When a reply is cut off at max_tokens, the loop retries it with four times the output cap, and it never checks whether the budget has room for that. The wrap-up check then compares that inflated worst case against the run's wrap-up line, so it sends the wrap-up at about a fifth of the budget spent.

Step by step:
(1) The run gets the small-budget output cap of 4096 by design (loop.ts:542-552 with WRITE_MAX_TOKENS_PER_CALL; ADR 0112 amendment 3 says "a small budget keeps 4,096 and its reserve does not grow").
(2) The model's first write of several files runs past 4096 tokens. In the live log, seq 42 and seq 35 each hold four write_file calls, and stop_reason is max_tokens. U-085 handling at loop.ts:767-783 throws the whole paid reply away, including the write_file blocks that were complete. It then sets cutOffFloor = min(maxOut*4, 32000) = 16384.
(3) On the next call, loop.ts:527-531 makes floor = max(maxTokensPerCall, cutOffFloor) = 16384. Because the ceiling (16384) is not above the floor, the room fitting at loop.ts:537-552 is skipped, and the retry goes out at 16384 whatever the budget.
(4) budget.ts:216-220 sends the wrap-up when runSpent + lineEstimate > line. The 16384-token worst case is about USD 0.164 on Sonnet 5.5 ($10/Mtok output) and the line is about USD 0.164. So at a spend of about USD 0.044-0.05, the check answers wrap_up. The precheck caps still allow the call, because 0.05 + 0.17 < 0.25.
(5) loop.ts:587-602 adds WRAP_UP_TEXT ("About a fifth ... is left. Start nothing new") to the retry request itself. That request holds only the three read results, because the cut reply was dropped. The model obeys and writes nothing.
(6) At executor.ts:1435, wrapUpSent plus a non-empty "Left to do" makes the task paused at its budget. The person sees "spent CHF 0.05 and listed 11 things left to do" and a Continue card.

cutOffFloor is also never reset, so every later call in the run keeps the 4x worst case. That brings the wrap-up early even for larger caps. At a USD 0.30 cap the retry ran without the wrap-up, but the next call carried it at USD 0.049 spent.

I reproduced this with the real LoopAgentDriver, the fake provider and Sonnet 5.5 pricing, with a USD 0.25 cap (CHF 0.20). The log line was 163,804 µUSD and the reserve 86,196 µUSD (CHF 0.13 and 0.07, as in the live log). max_tokens per call was [4096, 4096, 16384, 16384]. WRAP_UP_SENT came at a spend of 43,581 µUSD, and the retry request carried the wrap-up text. Live numbers agree: model-calls seq 40-43 for run bb83a69e (calls 4096/4096/4096/16384, the third cut at 4096 output) and seq 33-36 for the CHF 0.24 run.
verified.where: packages/runtime/src/agent/loop.ts:527-531 (cutOffFloor raised into the floor, which skips the room fitting at 537-552) and loop.ts:767-783 (the retry cap is min(maxOut*4, 32000) with no budget check, the cut reply including its complete tool calls is discarded, and cutOffFloor is never reset). Trigger: packages/runtime/src/enforcement/budget.ts:216-220 (runSpent + lineEstimate > line). Fixed wrap-up wording: loop.ts:86-87 (WRAP_UP_TEXT). Pause: packages/runtime/src/session/executor.ts:1435.
verified.fix_sketch:
1) In loop.ts, treat the raised cut-off limit as the target for one retry, not as a floor. On the retry, set maxOut = fitMaxTokens(priceAt, prevMaxOut, min(prevMaxOut*4, top), room). Here room = min(hooks.callRoomUsdMicro(ctx), line.lineUsdMicro - budget.spentByRunId(runId)), with line from req.budget.lineFor(...), so the retry's worst case stays below the wrap-up line. For the live run that is about 11-12k tokens, enough for the four files. Only when nothing above prevMaxOut fits is the run really at its line; then the wrap-up (or the error) applies as today. Reset cutOffFloor after the first reply that is not cut, so later calls go back to the room-fitted cap and the worst case of every later call does not stay 4x.
2) Better still, keep the complete tool_use blocks of a cut reply. Every block before the last one has parsed input (a cut block has _unparsed or never closes). Run those, and ask again only for the rest, so the USD 0.044 already paid is not wasted. This is an amendment to the U-085 rule.
3) Make WRAP_UP_TEXT say what is really left, for example "About N% of this task's budget is left", computed from cap minus spent. Or send it only when spent + the call's expected cost (not the inflated worst case) passes the line. This needs an ADR 0112 amendment, because the ADR fixes the wording.
4) Update ADR 0112 (amendment 3 / U-085 note) and the agent-loop maintainer doc.

Is it the model alone? No. Writing several files in one reply and obeying "Start nothing new" are both normal, expected model behaviour.

Downstream harm: each run recorded a wrong lesson ("Reading first used the budget the code needed"), and memory had 4 lessons by the next run. Those lessons can steer later briefs toward skipping the reads.

The ADR's own example ("more than a fifth is usually left") assumes the worst case stays near the 4096-token cap; the 4x retry breaks that assumption. Any coder budget below about USD 0.33 (CHF 0.26) on Sonnet 5.5 gets the wrap-up at the cut-off retry, or right after it.

The finding is real: pressing Stop now teaches the cost learner. Since the R-estimates fix, the plan card (`GET /inbox` planTasks, server.ts:1809) and the Start dialog (start-check.ts:78) both price tasks with the live learned estimate, `planEstimateUsdMicro(rt.estimates, task)`. Between the card and the dialog, that learner took a sample from the person's Stop now. The runner calls `onTaskFinished` with `result.outcome === "killed"` (runner.ts:1722, 1797), and the compose hook passes that outcome to `estimates.observeTaskRuns` (compose.ts:2665). `observeTaskRuns` leaves out only the outcomes in `NO_SAMPLE_CALL_OUTCOMES`: paused, budget_exceeded and usage_limit (model.ts:215, 753). `killed` is not in that list. The killed Run row also counts as a finished work run that did not stop at a budget, so `isNoSample` (model.ts:352) is false.

What the live run's state.sqlite shows:
- Reviewer task: est_cost_usd_micro 45000, budget 0. No reviewer key had any sample before, so the ratio was 1. The card showed 45000 USD x 0.8 = CHF 0.036, shown as 0.04.
- The first run is `killed` after 3 s, with 9561 + 2452 = 12013 USD micro booked in the ledger.

When that times out, Playwright's own cleanup in `_innerLaunch` / `_launchProcess` runs `closeOrKill(DEFAULT_PLAYWRIGHT_TIMEOUT = 30 s)`: it sends Browser.close over the pipe, waits up to 30 s, then sends SIGKILL to the process group (the browser is spawned detached). The client sees the rejection at 60 s and the server keeps cleaning up for up to 30 s more, so a browser that never starts lives for about 90 s in total and then dies.

The live timeline matches this. leftover-hung-browser-ps.txt has mtime 04:18:09.86 and shows `sleep 300` with etime 01:23, so it was spawned at about 04:16:47. The launch timed out at about 04:17:47 and Playwright's SIGKILL was due at about 04:18:17. The snapshot was taken 23 s after the timeout, which is inside the 30 s grace and about 7 s before the kill. The "78 s after the try gave up" figure is wrong.

I reproduced it twice:
- (a) Raw Playwright 1.64.1 with an `exec sleep` executable and a 3 s timeout: pw:browser logs `<gracefully close start>` at the timeout, then `<kill>` / `<will force kill>` / `signal=SIGKILL` exactly 30 s later.
- (b) The real `tryPages` from try-page.ts, run with tsx and FORERUNNER_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE set to the hung script: the result came at +60 s ('the browser did not start (browserType.launch: Timeout 60000ms exceeded.)'), the process was still listed at +60 to +85 s, and it was gone at +90 s. Nothing was left over.

If the daemon quits first, Playwright's exit handler also kills the browser.

The secondary claim, the raw Playwright text in the drawer, is accurate but is a separate copy item, not this bug. try-page.ts:224 and :232 append `firstLine(e)` ('browserType.launch: Timeout 60000ms exceeded.'). That goes against docs/design/core-experience.md copy rule 8 ('Errors are one sentence of what went wrong plus what to do ... not the exception text') and rule 6 (no module names). It is deliberate R-sandbox wording, pinned by packages/capabilities/test/try-page.test.ts:148.

The estimator never looks at what a task asks for. `EstimateModel.estimate` (packages/runtime/src/estimates/model.ts:515-537) prices a task from only two inputs: its specialist and its risk tier. When the task has no estimate of its own, the base is the specialist's flat starting figure (coder USD 0.04, :150-161). That base is then multiplied by a ratio learned per (specialist, tier) (`kindOfTask`, :233-237). `planEstimateUsdMicro` (:773-783) passes no title, outcome or criteria to it. A task made with New task never gets an estimate of its own: POST /projects/:id/tasks (packages/runtime/src/daemon/server.ts:1050-1072) writes no est_cost_usd_micro, and the DB row has 0. A plan task's own guess is clamped to 1.5x the flat figure (PLAN_ESTIMATE_BOUND, :169 and :185-196), so a coder task can never be estimated above USD 0.06 (about CHF 0.05).

I reproduced the exact figure with tsx on the code at 7d54fff. I fed in the live run's three coder/tier1 samples: the quote page's two tries, 62,690 and 104,364 against 60,000, and summary.md, 11,031 against 40,000. The result is 33,192 µUSD (ratio 0.8298, about CHF 0.03). That matches the session.planned event in state.sqlite. A one-line coder task gets the identical figure. In this run every coder task's Start dialog said "about CHF 0.03", from "Add a footer" to the Swiss tool and the round-robin scheduler.

What the work really cost (cost_ledger): one clean pass of this five-file task was USD 0.071 of work (one write call alone was 3,967 output tokens, USD 0.042) plus USD 0.036 for its review. That is about CHF 0.085, about 2.8x the estimate; the work alone is 2.1x.

Two other things widen the gap, but neither is the estimate's fault:
- The first run was cut off at 4,096 output tokens and wrapped up with nothing written (USD 0.044 lost, the small-budget output cap and the wrap-up timing).
- The critic sent the work back because players.json was missing (the model's choice).

There is also a like-for-like problem in the session review. Its "CHF 0.17 spent of a CHF 0.05 estimate" compares spend that includes reviews (USD 0.069 of 0.215) with an estimate that leaves reviews out (2 x 33,192 after the retry was replanned; packages/critic/src/session-review.ts:450-451, runner.ts:1411). verified.root_cause:
The try extractor turns a criterion that describes its argument in words into a bare command, and the critic then correctly refuses to let the model overrule a measured problem. In detail:

(1) Criterion 1, "node wc.js on a file containing 'hello world foo' prints 3", has no backticks, so it goes through the prose path of `commandsIn` and `parseCommand` (exact=false). The first argument word is "on". It is not argument-shaped, but it is in STOP_WORDS (try-plan.ts:126-130). So the loop at try-plan.ts:321-333 breaks with kept=[], and the command becomes `node wc.js` with no arguments. I reproduced this at the base with tsx: `commandsIn(criterion1)` returns words ["node","wc.js"]. `planTries` with the live brief returns two tries: `node wc.js` (from an acceptance criterion, expectsError=false) and `node wc.js <file>` (from the brief). Criteria are read before the brief (try-plan.ts:146-148), so the bare form is not deduped against `node wc.js <file>`; the dedupe key is the exact word list.

(2) `expectsError` (try-plan.ts:449-452) reads only the command's own sentence, criterion 1, which has no error words. Criterion 4 ("Running with no argument prints a usage message to stderr and exits with code 1") is never consulted. So the usage exit becomes "problem: it exited with code 1" in try-run.ts:166-169, with ok=false and blocking=true.

(3) `buildVerdict` (packages/critic/src/critic.ts:829-836) turns every blocking try into a high finding "Tried node wc.js: …". `applyVerdictRules` (rules.ts:205) then turns accept into revise. By ADR 0104 (measured.ts:3-11) a measured finding is closed only by a new measurement, never by the model's accept or its resolved list. Every retry measures the same bare run again, because the criteria are fixed. The coder cannot remove the finding: ADR 0110 rejected guessing a no-argument run for exactly this reason ("a usage message with a non-zero exit would be a finding the task cannot remove"). The code contradicts its own ADR, which also says "A command whose words end in a guess … is not run".

The critic's accept (seq 70, 77, 84: grade 93/93/90, each saying the problem is the expected usage exit) was overridden three times. The ladder then went to Opus, and the fourth report asked the person. The override itself is by design and should stay; the defect is the try it was given.

Secondary, cosmetic but real: the session log's "<file" with no ">" comes from `quotedWords` (packages/critic/src/followup.ts:98). Its `.replace(/[*`#>]+/g, "")` removes every ">" as if it were markdown. Verified: `quotedWords('Sent back: Tried node wc.js: … Usage: node wc.js <file>. …', 100)` returns '… Usage: node wc.js <file.'
verified.where: packages/runtime/src/loop/try-plan.ts:321-333 (prose command ends at stop word "on" with no args; STOP_WORDS at :126-130); try-plan.ts:449-452 (expectsError reads only the command's own sentence); enforcement by design at packages/critic/src/critic.ts:829-836 + packages/critic/src/rules.ts:205; cosmetic cut at packages/critic/src/followup.ts:98
verified.fix_sketch:
1. try-plan.ts `parseCommand`, prose path: split STOP_WORDS into verbs ("prints", "outputs", "exits", "shows", …) and connectors or prepositions ("on", "with", "for", "in", "from", "at", "by", "to", "as", …). If the command reaches a connector before any argument was kept ("node wc.js on a file containing …", "node wc.js with a file …"), the sentence describes the arguments rather than writing them, so return null and the command is not run, as ADR 0110 requires. A simpler rule that has the same effect: run a prose command with no arguments only when the next word is a verb ("node wc.js prints usage").

2. Defence in `planTries`: drop a no-argument prose command for a script that some text also names with written arguments (the brief's or README's `node wc.js <file>`). Also, for a try with argv length 2, set `expectsError` when any criterion, the brief or the README says /\b(?:no|without (?:an?|any)?)\s+(?:arguments?|file|input)\b/ next to usage, error or exit-non-zero words. Then a bare run that the criteria ask to fail is "(the brief expects an error here)" and is not counted as a problem.

3. Keep the ADR 0104 rule in critic.ts that a measured problem blocks accept. Do not let the model's accept overrule a try; fix what is tried.

4. followup.ts:98: strip only a leading blockquote marker (e.g. `.replace(/^\s*>+\s?/gm, "")` before whitespace is collapsed), not every ">", so "<file>" survives in cards and the session log.

5. Amend ADR 0110 point 1 and docs/maintainers (critic or verification doc): a command whose arguments are described in words is not run.

(1) Write room (loop.ts:545-553). A run that can write files and names no ceiling gets this room: min(hooks room, max(WRAP_UP_SHARE*cap/WRAP_UP_CALLS, priceAt(floor))). That is a flat tenth of the run cap per call. On Sonnet 5.5, 16,384 output tokens alone cost USD 0.164, so no run under about USD 1.7 can ever get the whole-file room. This run's cap was CHF 0.48 = USD 0.60 (line CHF 0.38, reserve CHF 0.10, per the task.step event), so the room was USD 0.06. By seq 6 the context made even the 4,096-token floor cost more than that (seq 8 billed 38,465 cached + 7,527 written + 4,096 output = USD 0.0675). fitMaxTokens therefore returned the floor (loop.ts:1150) and the 8 KB comparison.md write was cut off. loop-cache.test.ts:236 and ADR 0112 amendment 3 ("a small budget keeps 4,096") pin this as intended.

(2) Cut-off retry (loop.ts:770-781 with 528-531 and 542). After the cut-off, cutOffFloor = min(maxOut*4, model limit or 32k) becomes the floor of every later call. When floor >= ceiling, the `ceiling > floor` branch is skipped and the room is never consulted; when nothing fits, fitMaxTokens returns the floor anyway. So the retry (seq 9) and all later calls (seq 10-12) asked 16,384 tokens, with worst cases around USD 0.17. That is about 3x the write room. Only the hard run-cap precheck limits them, and it is not even limited by `ceiling` (the repro raised it to 22,428 tokens, above WRITE_MAX_TOKENS_PER_CALL).

The run never keeps the limit that cut the write: it pays for the thrown-away reply (USD 0.0675, 15% of the run's USD 0.444) and then pays for the large call anyway. A 16,384 cap at seq 8 would have passed every check: USD 0.130 spent + about USD 0.19 worst case is under the USD 0.48 line.

At 4,096 tokens it would have been 0.369 + about 0.051, under the line.
